description: Generates an AI image on the signed-in aicut account and puts the aicut card in front of the user. It waits for the image server-side for as long as one request safely can - about 20 seconds - so it usually returns the finished image with its `url` directly. WHEN: the user asks for an image. Call `list_models` first if you have not this session - the `model` id and the allowed values for every other argument come from there, and a combination it does not publish is rejected. AFTER: check `status`. If it is `succeeded` the image is finished - go straight to the SHOW rule below. If it is `queued` or `processing`, the image was not ready in time and is still being made: call `wait_for_generation` with the returned id and `media: "image"`, then follow both rules below. THE CARD: this call has ALREADY put the aicut card in front of the user, and it fills in the finished media on its own. Do NOT call `show_generation` for this job - that adds a duplicate card; it is only for bringing back an EARLIER generation. HOW TO WAIT: call `wait_for_generation` with this job's id and `media` - it waits server-side and opens no card. While it answers `terminal: false`, wait `poll_after_seconds` and call it again; when `terminal: true`, tell the user in ONE short line what came out. Do not poll `get_video` / `get_image` / `get_audio` instead or spawn timers, and do NOT tell the user the generation is running in between. IF YOU CANNOT RENDER AN AICUT CARD (a terminal or plain SDK client), give the user the `url` from the wait result - aicut cannot see which clients render cards. TIMING: an image usually finishes in under 90 seconds, and can take up to about 4 minutes. `generate_image` waits about 20 seconds for it server-side; if it returns while the image is still `processing`, call `wait_for_generation` rather than waiting in a timer or a background shell. COST: this spends the user's tokens. Pass `estimate_only: true` first to get the exact price without creating anything - and do that whenever the user has not already agreed to the cost, or when the balance may be tight. SPENDS TOKENS: quote it first (`estimate_only: true`), state the price IN THE SAME MESSAGE as your ask, and wait for a go that names THIS purchase - a bare 'yes' counts only as the direct answer to that priced ask, and an ambiguous one means ask again. The full SPENDING RULES in this server's instructions apply here. IF THE USER REPORTS A CHARGE OR STEP THEY DID NOT EXPECT: re-read your own tool calls and say which you made; aicut cards cannot spend (full rule in this server's instructions). IDEMPOTENCY: `idempotency_key` is optional. Reusing a key REPLAYS the job it first created (even with different settings), so never reuse one to make another generation; the full rules are in this server's instructions (IDEMPOTENCY). OUTPUT: JSON for you to read. Tell the user the media URL plus a one-line summary; do not paste raw JSON, job ids or internal field names.

aspect_ratio.description: Output aspect ratio, one of the model's published `aspect_ratios` (for example `9:16`).

estimate_only.description: Price these exact settings and create nothing. Returns the token cost, the account balance, and whether the balance covers it. Costs nothing and changes nothing.

idempotency_key.description: Optional retry-safety key. Read the IDEMPOTENCY note in this tool's description before using one - a reused key returns the first job instead of making a new one.

images.description: URLs of input images to edit or use as references, on the models that accept them. Either public https URLs (aicut fetches and stores them) or URLs earlier generations on this same account returned.

model.description: Model id, exactly as `list_models` returns it (for example `nano-banana-2`). Models differ in price by more than any other setting, so use the one the user asked for and never substitute a cheaper model to save them tokens.

prompt.description: What the image should show. The model's `prompt` parameter in `list_models` gives its character limit.

quality.description: Quality tier, on the models that publish a `quality` parameter. Higher tiers cost more. Never set this to save the user tokens or to make a generation cheaper - set it only when the user explicitly asked for this value, and never carry it over from an earlier request.

resolution.description: Output resolution, one of the model's published options (for example `1k`). Higher resolutions cost more. Never set this to save the user tokens or to make a generation cheaper - set it only when the user explicitly asked for this value, and never carry it over from an earlier request.
